bc_krack_rock.blurb: A compact crag in the Smoke Bluffs at Squamish, set right beside the parking area so the walk in takes under five minutes. Most of the climbing is single-pitch traditional, with lines running roughly 10 to 30 metres, plus a couple of bolted or mixed options. The nine climbs here spread fairly evenly from 5.7 up to 5.10, which suits climbers building up their gear-placing experience. Bring a full trad rack.

bc_cabin_boy_s_office.blurb: A small crag within the Smoke Bluffs at Squamish with nine routes between 5.8 and 5.10, most of them at the 5.10 level. The lines are mainly traditional, so a rack is needed, though one bolted sport line sits among them and some routes combine gear with a bolt or two. With only one climb below 5.9, it is better suited to climbers already comfortable on 5.10 than to those just starting out on trad.

bc_ice_box.blurb: A single boulder in the Sleight of Hand sector of Hunter Creek, in the Fraser Valley, holding nine problems that run from V5 up to V9, with the bulk at V7 and above. It is reached by continuing past the far end of the neighbouring Sleight of Hand boulder along a well-worn path. One face stays shaded in the morning by a larger boulder beside it, which helps on warm days, and the other side stays in shade for most of the day. Expect a hard, steep, scooped-face style of climbing.

bc_lost_pebbles_boulders.blurb: A small cluster of lower boulders in the Gold Rush zone of the Fraser Canyon, a short stretch up the highway from Yale. Nine problems range from V1 to V4, so it works as an easy warm-up spot or a place for newer boulderers. The trees give plenty of shade, which makes it a pleasant choice on hot summer days. From where you leave the car it is roughly a minute on a faint trail into the forest, and the entrance can grow over.

bc_tranquility_boulder.blurb: A large boulder close to the main trail in the Campbell Lake Trail boulder group near Harrison Hot Springs in the Fraser Valley. It carries nine problems spanning V0 to V6, with the greatest concentration around V4 and just one problem at V6. The easier V0 to V3 lines make it a reasonable stop for newer boulderers, while the V4 cluster gives stronger climbers several options on the same boulder.
